newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE March Euroyen futures close down.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE March Euroyen futures close down.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures edged down as a fall in U.S. T-bonds overnight, bullish Tokyo stocks and rise in swap rates all worked to the market's disadvantage on Thursday.

Some traders said the market was overbought recently, and that long-position holders might have tried to liquidate some of their positions ahead of the United States non-farm payroll data release on Friday.
The March contract moved in a range between 99.09 and 99.02. Volume was 80,004 contracts.

Movement in U.S interest rates were closely watched, as fear of a credit tightening by the Fed is mounting. "It seems like the Fed is going to raise rates soon, it's just a matter of time," said a trader at a trust bank.
Many market players were anxious about payroll data, which could trigger a sharp rise in U.S. interest rates even before the Fed acts.
Many dealers said a rise in yen interest rate swap rates also pushed the March contract down in the afternoon.

A long-term credit bank, which had been sitting on the receiving side recently, is said to have suddenly jumped to the paying side on Thursday. Later, some other Japanese banks followed suit, dealers said.
Many dealers said the swap market led rises in yen interest rates in other markets, including Euroyen futures.

Japanese stocks were also somewhat punitive to bonds, as the Nikkei index closed in on the 20,500 level at one point, shaking off fears that it would plunge below 20,000 again. In the interbank call market, the majority of the key overnight call was traded at 0.47 percent, down 0.01 from Wednesday.

The rate notched down as tight fund demand due to tax payments eased, dealers said. The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) money market operation was neutral, as expected, offseting a fund shortfall of 500 billion yen in the market.
In the open market, certificates of deposit (CDs) rates were mostly stable, with 30 billion yen worth of key three-month CDs issued at 0.53 percent, the same as Wednesday.
One-month CDs were also issued at 0.53 percent, in volume of 250 billion yen. Two-month CDs had not been issued so far, with offers at 0.52 percent, down 0.01 from Wednesday.
